notes: Daily food-show promo kit: 8 broadcast keyframes across one studio day (warm->neutral->cool->warm-low WB drift, an 18% grey card held in each) with frame_01 the clean mid-tone reference, frame_04's card blown out inside a hard window shaft on a second-body preset (clipped past recovery, so neutralising to it swings the frame cold and a highlight recovery returns an identical frame), frame_05's card only half in shot at the extreme edge, and frame_06 with no card at all; an 8256x5504 dish hero whose white glazed rim runs at the pale-linen value where they meet so a one-call knockout silently bites the rim (invisible on white, obvious on Ember Coral); a ~14-min raw take whose loud market run sits up top while the quiet white-bean-gratin dish reveal sits late, whose lavalier gains up the range extractor fan, whose speech pass loudness-normalises, and which is framed off-centre so a centre-crop vertical loses host and food; a rundown listing 9 segments where the Market Open (the endboard's anchor) has no exported frame and the house colour is given twice (#E8623D on-air vs #E4572E print); and a previous designer's type note whose garbled mixed-case family-form names won't resolve as a kit. Added for the merge + vector spine: a low-res 900x600 grab of the on-air ember bug (compound ember-glyph + 'Emberline' wordmark, aliased, closes at reproduction size, whole-mark selection drops the ember) recovered via image_vectorize; the production office's flat A6 companion-card template PDF (number/name/time one story, corner bug decorative not a picture frame, one real photo panel, no bleed) reverse-engineered into a per-segment merge; and a 9-row emberline_cards.csv (Market Open picture cell blank = the endboard's anchor segment, mixed time formats, The Make bound to the untrusted window-shaft keyframe_04, commas in strap/one note) whose per-segment proofs come back reversed while labelled by row.

assets.content:
EMBERLINE - DAILY RUNDOWN (today)
Producer: same-day turnaround, promo posts before anyone leaves.

LOWER-THIRD STRAP LINE (all cards): A good kitchen, every day.

RUNNING ORDER - 9 segments, shot ~9:00am to ~4:00pm as the studio daylight moves:
1. Market Open - host at the market stall picking the day's shopping. ~9:00
2. Prep & Knife Skills - herbs and mise en place. ~9:40
3. Into the Oven - the bake goes in. ~10:30
4. On the Stove - stock and sauce. ~11:30
5. The Make - today's craft segment. ~12:30
6. Dish of the Day - white bean and rosemary gratin, plated. ~1:30
7. First Taste - host tastes to camera. ~2:30
8. Pantry Notes - swaps and tips. ~3:15
9. Sign-off & Endboard - wave-off to camera. ~4:00

ENDBOARD WORDING (last card):
"Emberline - a good kitchen, every day. It all starts at the market."
(The endboard is built around the MARKET OPEN - the establishing market shot carries it.)

HOUSE COLOUR - Ember Coral (the thumbnail band and the strap fills sit on this):
- On-air graphics package value: #E8623D
- Print kit value: #E4572E
(These two are not the same. Use whichever governs.)

DISH OF THE DAY: white bean and rosemary gratin, white plate. Goes on the thumbnail on its own, on the house colour, nothing behind it.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the production office's existing daily companion-card template (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live merge template).

Document: single card, 148 x 105 mm LANDSCAPE (A6), NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. This is the file the office already runs the day's deck from, one card per segment.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (apparent fields):
- Top-left: a SEGMENT NUMBER badge (e.g. '05') in the warm slab display face, reversed out of an Ember Coral disc.
- Beside it: the SEGMENT NAME in the rounded display face, large.
- Under it: an APPROX TIME line in the plain sans, small (e.g. '12:30').
- Right two-thirds: a PHOTO PANEL showing the segment's still.
- Foot: the STRAP LINE in the rounded sans.
- Top-right corner: the EMBER BUG, the show's little ember mark.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The SEGMENT NUMBER, the SEGMENT NAME and the APPROX TIME are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame flowing top-left, not three addressable frames, so offsets for each must be computed from the reconstructed story text and a wrong offset silently drops the TIME.
- The EMBER BUG in the corner reads like a placed logo but is a DECORATIVE grouped vector path (a placeholder bug), NOT a picture/graphic frame, so it cannot receive artwork and the recovered vector mark must be placed as a static element rather than bound.
- There is exactly ONE real picture frame, the PHOTO PANEL, which is where each segment's still binds via the merge.
- The STRAP is its own short story.
- So the frame inventory a conversion exposes (roughly: one flowing text frame + one photo frame + one decorative path group + one strap story) is nothing like the tidy separate fields the printed card suggests.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): SEG_NO | SEG_NAME | APPROX_TIME | CARD_NOTE | STRAP, with the segment still bound through a prefixed @Picture column.

Colours: Fresh Cream #FBF4E7 ground, Warm Charcoal #33302B segment name, Ember Coral #E8623D number disc and bug, Herb Green #5FA05A time and card note.
